content:
This week, Apple continued its steady expansion of its Apple Sports app, broadening its football coverage while also offering tennis fans new ways to follow major tournaments. Here are the latest updates.

Apple Sports adds several new football leagues and tennis draws

When Apple first launched the Apple Sports app, the experience was quite limited in terms of both regional availability and the sports covered.

Since then, the app has continued to grow in both respects, expanding its coverage to over 170 countries and regions while gradually adding support for new sports, leagues, and events.

For example, earlier this year, Apple Sports expanded into 90 new countries and added a number of features for the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports received another update, with Australian A-League Men, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League, and South African Premier League joining the football lineup.

In addition, Apple said the app now lets tennis fans "follow live draws... including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events," allowing users to "see matchups and results for each round at a glance."

Below is the full release notes for Apple Sports 4.4:

The football lineup continues to expand with the addition of Australian A-League Men, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League, and South African Premier League. Tennis fans can now follow live draws on Apple Sports, covering brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events, with a clear view of matchups and results for each round.

Are you using Apple Sports? Let us know in the comments.
